audit.whatIsWrong: Row 0 read Vladimir at 8/10 while whys[0] and early both say level 1 is even; rows 4, 5 and 6 read Skill while whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] all say Vladimir keeps the lane. The packet chart is Skill then Vladimir x6.
audit.why: The chart and the prose disagreed on four of seven rows, and the packet agrees with the prose on all four.
audit.corrected: Row 0 to Skill, rows 4-6 to Vladimir, in matched full/content pairs, ratings adjusted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns; 'Heart Zapper's cooldown' anchored ten instructions with no number attached.
audit.why: Heart Zapper 17/16.5/16/15.5/15, Infected Bonesaw 4s at 975 range, Blunt Force Trauma 9s, Maximum Dosage 120s. The 17s Heart Zapper is when your Grievous Wounds has to already be on him.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into phases[0], phases[3], phases[4], spikes[1], mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two facts were missing. Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilizing effect — and Vladimir's kit contains no immobilize at all, only slows on W and E, so the cannister never triggers off you. Blunt Force Trauma's auto reset was never flagged as the burst tell.
audit.why: This is the most under-stated fact in the lane: the passive that makes Dr. Mundo frustrating for the rest of the map is simply inert against Vladimir solo, and it only comes up when your jungler arrives. Heart Zapper's healing off stored damage is also the specific reason anti-heal timing matters, rather than a generic 'his healing'.
audit.corrected: Passive interaction written into report[5]; the auto-reset tell and Heart Zapper's stored-damage healing written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].

edits.before: Q-drain on cooldown — you trade HP like a loan shark. Identify how Dr. Mundo contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is even. Infected Bonesaw is 975 range on a 4s cooldown, so take the chip at max range and heal it back with Transfusion.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Heart Zapper's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Free-farm window: Heart Zapper is 17s and heals off the damage it stored, so have Grievous Wounds on him before any extended trade.

edits.before: Hemoplague + empowered Q turns mid-game fights into resets. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Dr. Mundo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Level 6 is still yours — Maximum Dosage heals a share of his missing health on 120s, but it only saves him; it never turns a trade.

edits.before: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Heart Zapper's cooldown.
edits.after: Riftmaker is your spike — Hemoplague's amp on a huge health bar is what shreds him.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Dr. Mundo carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: your amp and sustained magic damage out-scale his stacking outright. Close before the map decides.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Heart Zapper: 17s at rank 1 — it heals off the damage he stored, so anti-heal before the burst. - Blunt Force Trauma: 9s auto reset; the wind-up is the tell. - Maximum Dosage: 120s. - Sanguine Pool: 28s. - Hemoplague: 120s.

edits.before: Track Dr. Mundo's Heart Zapper: His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. When it is down — Q-E + R him.
edits.after: Your kit has no immobilize, so his cannister passive never triggers off you — only off your jungler.

edits.before: His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Heart Zapper heals off the damage it stored. Anti-heal before the burst lands.

edits.before: His Maximum Dosage (R) is a big heal and MS burst that makes him nearly unkillable solo, but it doesn't out-trade your poke over a lane. Don't try to all-in him through R — just keep chipping and denying CS; you're favoured because he can't punish you.
edits.after: His Maximum Dosage (R) is a 120s heal of his missing health plus move speed that makes him nearly unkillable solo, but it never out-trades your poke over a lane. Don't all-in through R — keep chipping and denying CS; you are favoured because he cannot punish you.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay firmly in your favour. His Maximum Dosage (R) keeps him alive but never lets him actually punish you — you can't easily kill him, but he can't kill you either, so you free-farm, take plates, and poke with Tides (E). Deny his cleaver last-hits and starve his stacking.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay firmly in your favour. Maximum Dosage keeps him alive but never lets him punish you, and Heart Zapper heals off stored damage every 17s — put Oblivion Orb on him before you commit. Free-farm, take plates, poke with Tides (E), and starve his stacking.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES — Maximum Dosage is the correct name. UNVERIFIED: the page claims three times that Infected Bonesaw 'costs him max HP'. Riot's description in the kit file gives no health cost and the cost field reads 0, so I neither repeated nor removed the claim; it needs a source before it is trusted.
